name: Elacestrant (oral SERD for ESR1-mutated mBC, EMERALD)
cyclesNote: Cycled every 28 days continuously until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

source.nccn: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Invasive Breast Cancer v6.2026
source.primaryStudy: EMERALD: Bidard FC, Kaklamani VG, Neven P, et al. J Clin Oncol 2022;40:3246-3256; Bardia A, et al. Clin Cancer Res 2024;30:4299-4309

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (NCCN v6.2026 BINV-Q 6, 14 of 15)

biomarkers.note: Requires ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer with confirmed ESR1 mutation (detected by blood ctDNA or tissue NGS) following disease progression on at least one line of endocrine therapy containing a CDK4/6 inhibitor. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Invasive Breast Cancer v6.2026, BINV-Q (6 of 15 and 14 of 15).

supportiveCare: Administration: take with food at approximately the same time each day to reduce nausea and dyspepsia.
Nausea and dyspepsia management: consider standard antiemetics or acid-suppressive therapy if symptomatic.
Lipid monitoring: monitor fasting lipids (hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia can occur).
monitoring: Fasting lipid panel (total cholesterol, triglycerides) at baseline and periodically during therapy
CBC and liver function tests before starting and periodically
Monitor for musculoskeletal pain, nausea, and vomiting each cycle
clearanceChecks: confirmed ESR1 mutation on ctDNA or tissue biopsy

doseModificationRules.text: Hold elacestrant until recovery to grade ≤ 1. Resume at reduced dose level: first reduction 258 mg PO daily; second reduction 172 mg PO daily. Discontinue if unable to tolerate 172 mg daily.

drugs.name: Elacestrant
drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v6.2026, BINV-Q 14 of 15. Elacestrant 345 mg PO once daily with food on Days 1 to 28 of each 28-day cycle.
